Deck Name : Meat Puppets Jumping at Shadows
Author : Norman S. Brown Jr
Description :
The deck functions around getting a vampire with supeior viccitude to
bauble a Assault Rifle onto a vampire with superior Obtenebration. The
vampire with the superior Obtenebration and the Assault Rifle then
Descends into Darkness. While the vampire with Assault Rifle is out of
play the baubled vampire burns the bauble. During your influence phase
the vampire with the Descent into Darkeness gains two blood and
returns to play with the now FREE ASSAULT RIFLE! Shennanigans ensue.

Crypt [12 vampires] Capacity min: 4 max: 7 average: 5.67
------------------------------------------------------------

1x Henri Lavenant 7 DOM OBT pot qui Lasombra:3
1x Kazimir Savostin 7 AUS VIC ani pot Tzimisce:3
1x Omme Enberbenight 7 MYT OBT cel dom priscus Kiasyd:4

1x Otieno 6 OBT POT ani dom Lasombra:4

1x Andrew Emory 5 OBT aus dom pot bishop Lasombra:4
1x Dame Hollerton 5 DOM OBT myt Kiasyd:4
1x Ermenegildo, The R 5 DOM OBT pot Lasombra:4

I saw a version of this deck that also used Corporal Reservoir for
additional blood gain through Descent. Tap the Reservoirs before
Descending, gain the blood, and then they come back untapped once you
return from the Darkness.

You might consider dropping the War Ghoul angle, since Assault Rifles
will likely be sufficient. I think your key minion could be Ramiro,
who is cheap and Lasombra with vic (and you only need inferior.) I
would consider a crypt like this:
3x Ramiro
1x Christine Boscacci
1x Horatio
2x Henri Lavenant
2x Banjoko
1x Gratiano
1x Guido Lucciano
1x Talley, the Hound

Might consider a Shadow Play or two.

> Combat [10]
> 3x Arms of the Abyss
> 4x Shadow Body
> 3x Shadow Step

I like more Arms of the Abyss, because it's so good against anything
except grapple. Of course, if you maneuver with the gun, you can't
Arms of the Abyss. Therefore, I'd also suggest Darkness Within, since
it gives you a maneuver.

> Equipment [7]
> 7x Assault Rifle

> Master [12]
> 5x Blood Doll
> 2x Haven Uncovered
> 5x Wash

Seems like you could have more masters here, since you only effectly
have 7. If you like the Corporal Reservoir angle, you could replace
several Wash with them. I'd also add a Blooding or two for your
actions. I also like The Barrens to get rid of extra Assault Rifles
once you have what you need. Maybe Fame?

Ira

Messages.Author: Bram Vink
Messages.Body:

> Archon of the Swamp-

I think the main weakness of your deck is that when you have the
assault rifle, kazimir is a mismatch in your deck. So although he can
play the council and probably get the bauble done, it might be
worthwhile checking if it's not a better choice to retain a solid
minion after this, because the investment of 7 is a bit sketchy imo.
Robert Scythe made a great version of this deck, I would reccommend
taking a look at his iteration:
http://groups.google.com/group/rec.games.trading-cards.jyhad/browse_frm/thread/64861cea94b103f7/9d0ae7b7d00e0bfe

Another crypt option would be to try and combine similar spreads with
obt and/or vic.

for instance:

3x Nostoket: 8, obt ANI PRO Black Hand
2x Philippe: 7, obt ani PRO Black Hand
1x Tahibita: 4, obt pro
2x Jane Sims: 4, VIC ani pro
2x Horrock, 5, vic ANI PRO
2x Darvag, 8, VIC ANI pro Black Hand

Then perhaps with a few protean skill cards added. Heidelberg should
also assist with bloodmanagement. Obtenebration doesn't need to be
superior if you've got sufficient wakes and your only obt card is
descent.
Or perhaps a crypt based on matthew romans/the malk vic-guys (removing
the black hand angle)

Also, your bloodmanagement needs to be slightly more intensive. A lot
of your cards cost blood, and a one-turn descent only nets you one (5
corporal reservoirs do not change that by all that much) - I'd use
more corporals, or some perfectionist/hg/coven stuff.

Cheers,
B

As Bram mentioned, the deck I was remembering was built by Robert
Scythe.

> You really need superior Viccitude IMHO so that you can immediately
> burn the Bauble after your Lasombra descends into darkness. You then
> pop him back out during your influence phase.

It's my understanding that you can do this with inferior vic, due to
the card text on Bauble:

Bauble
vic: Put this card on the acting vampire. Search through your library
and put a non-unique, non-location equipment card on another minion
you control.Do not pay the cost to equip. The vampire with this card
cannot attempt actions, block or vote. You may burn this card and the
chosen equipment card during your untap phase or ****when the vampire
with the chosen equipment leaves the controlled region.****

Emphasis mine. When the vampire Descends, he leaves the controlled
region, and therefore you can burn the Bauble.

It seems like this deck has stirred up some stuff with the RT, since
they're going to review that ruling soon. :)

I think once you agree that inferior vic is sufficient, you'll have
better crypt options.

> an interesting twist, and depending on your meta that is fine, but as
> simple dodge beats an Assault Rifle at long.

Arms of the Abyss beats dodge, but you can't play Arms if you use the
manuever from the gun. Which is why I suggested Darkness Within, so
you could manuever with the Darkness, then Arms of the Abyss.

Ira

I don't think you understand Bauble very well, which is
understandable.

...The VAMPIRE WITH THIS CARD CANNOT ATTEMPT ACTIONS.... (emphasis
mine)

So the vampire with the Assault Rifle descends into Darkness and while
he is down there, the other vampire (the one with the bauble on him)
burns the bauble. The Assault Rifle is out of play. The Assault
Rifle is not affected by the Bauble in play being burned.

Superior Vissicitude is required so that you can burn the bauble
immediately so that you can immediately bring back your descended
vampire during your influence phase THIS TURN.

[vic] Put this card on the acting vampire. Search your library and put

a non-unique, non-location equipment card on another minion you

control. Do not pay the cost to equip. The vampire with this card

cannot attempt actions, block or vote. You may burn this card and the

chosen equipment card during your****untap phase***** or when the
minion with the chosen equipment leaves the controlled region.

[VIC] As above, but you may burn this card and the chosen equipment at
any time.

So all in one turn you can Bauble with vampire A, Descend with Assault
Rifle bearing vampire B, burn Bauble with vampire A, then during your
influence phase vampire B comes back into play, untapped with 2 more
blood, and the now FREE ASSAULT RIFLE.

If you have inferior vicissitude then have to wait until your untap
phase to burn the bauble.

If you have inferior obtenebratoin then you come back into play
tapped.

Comments Welcome,
Norman S. Brown, Jr
XZealot
Archon of the Swamp

uh, no Norm. Inferior vic is fine.

Vamp A plays bauble at vic, giving Assult rifle to vamp B.

Vamp B then Descends. Since Vamp B just descended (leaving the
controlled region), Vamp A can now (right now, this very same minion
phase) burn the bauble using the "when the minion with the chosen
equipment leaves the controlled region" clause of inferior vic. Since B
is out of play, the assault rifle stays.

Then that influence phase, you bring B back up, with an assault rifle.
With no Bauble around to stop vamp A doing stuff.

Just like you want.

Based on LSJ's reply, I understand that I was wrong. I don't
understand WHY I'm wrong, though.

1) Vampire Decends. The action resolves.
2) On the resolution of the action, the text on inferior bauble can be
triggered, since the vampire has left the controlled region.

1 must be complete before 2, and therefore I thought that burning the
bauble couldn't affect an out-of-play assault rifle.

Apparently the vampire isn't really uncontrolled yet, so the Assault
Rifle is still in play and would be burned. But that doesn't make
sense to me. From a game balance perspective, it's probably for the
best, though. :)

Looks like VIC it is.

Ira

So does this mean that "When X happens" should be read as "When X is
happening, but before it finishes happening?"

> But if you burn it on the next untap phase (or "at any time" later if
> superior), then it works. Currently. The lack of legal targets for
> the burn effect puts that ruling under review.

I think this is the "Legal Targets" ruling you are basing the review on:

> Playing Cards:
> If a card targets (chooses, selects, is played on, etc.) some
> target, then the card can only be played if an appropriate target is
> available. Examples: Strike: Steal/Destroy Equipment/Weapon cannot be
> used if the opposing minion doesn't have a suitable Equipment/Weapon
> to be destroyed/stolen. [RTR 19980928] [LSJ 20030408]

(If that's not correct, would you mind indicating what's prompting the
review? Assuming it is correct, for now...)

So, what is a target, exactly? It seems like it's something that you
choose. Note that the ruling on targeting cards seems to be about
choice. It even uses the words "chooses" and "selects." If I play
Strike: Destroy Equipment vs. an opponent who has multiple equipment, I
have to choose which one to destroy... thus I have to have a valid
choice, thus a valid choice must exist before I can choose it.

It doesn't seem that Bauble's burn clause involves choosing, selecting,
etc. It's "you burn this specific thing and that specific thing." If
the weapon is not controlled, it seems to be a case of being unable to
do the complete effect, so in such cases, don't you proceed by doing
what you can anyways? Like Blood to Water vs. a vampire with only two
blood?

If you really think this needs reviewing, would you consider reviewing
the following scenario also, or point out why it's dissimilar?

I play Blessing of the Name and choose three of my minions. By my next
untap phase, one of them becomes no longer controlled (such as with
Descent into Darkness.) Do we need to question whether the "burn this
card and tap the chosen minions" takes effect, since all of it's "targets"
(if they are indeed targets for that part of the effect) are not around?

>> Correct.
>
> So does this mean that "When X happens" should be read as "When X is
> happening, but before it finishes happening?"

It means when it happens, not later, yeah.

>> But if you burn it on the next untap phase (or "at any time" later if
>> superior), then it works. Currently. The lack of legal targets for
>> the burn effect puts that ruling under review.
>
> I think this is the "Legal Targets" ruling you are basing the review on:
>
>> Playing Cards:
>> If a card targets (chooses, selects, is played on, etc.) some
>> target, then the card can only be played if an appropriate target is
>> available. Examples: Strike: Steal/Destroy Equipment/Weapon cannot be
>> used if the opposing minion doesn't have a suitable Equipment/Weapon
>> to be destroyed/stolen. [RTR 19980928] [LSJ 20030408]
>
> (If that's not correct, would you mind indicating what's prompting the
> review? Assuming it is correct, for now...)
>
> So, what is a target, exactly? It seems like it's something that you
> choose.

It is the target of the effect. The thing the effect affects. The object of the
action.

The target of the action to burn an Army of Rats in the "burn this card" action
provided by Army of Rats is the Army of Rats card, even though there is no choice.

> Note that the ruling on targeting cards seems to be about
> choice.

It is not, nor should is seem that way. See the text you quoted. "targets

(chooses, selects, is played on, etc.)"

> It even uses the words "chooses" and "selects."

... and "is played on" and "etc." with no indication that the list of examples
is constraining in any way.

> If I play
> Strike: Destroy Equipment vs. an opponent who has multiple equipment, I
> have to choose which one to destroy... thus I have to have a valid
> choice, thus a valid choice must exist before I can choose it.

Yes.

And if he has only 1, you have no choice, but still must have a target.

If he has 0, you cannot play it, since there is nothing to target.

> It doesn't seem that Bauble's burn clause involves choosing, selecting,
> etc.

It doesn't involve choosing in the "among options" sense. It does involve
choosing in the select sense (or the identify sense).

It does selects the equipment. Selecting it for burning.
Targeting it. Burning it.

> It's "you burn this specific thing and that specific thing." If

"that thing" being the target of the effect of burning.

What is the target of the burn effect?
That thing.

> the weapon is not controlled, it seems to be a case of being unable to
> do the complete effect, so in such cases, don't you proceed by doing
> what you can anyways?

If the effect was being generated, yes.

Like an attempt to burn a weapon with superior Fractured Armament after the
weapon burned itself as a strike with first strike. The Fractured Armament
strike would still inflict 1 damage (even though the "burn equipment" part fizzles).

> Like Blood to Water vs. a vampire with only two
> blood?

Blood to Water targets the minion, not the blood.
It cannot be played if there is no minion to target.

> If you really think this needs reviewing, would you consider reviewing
> the following scenario also, or point out why it's dissimilar?

Dissimilarity: optional vs. mandatory (as in the Fractured Armament case --
allowed when it is mandatory, even if there is no equipment, but disallowed when
it is optional and there is no equipment).

> I play Blessing of the Name and choose three of my minions. By my next
> untap phase, one of them becomes no longer controlled (such as with
> Descent into Darkness.) Do we need to question whether the "burn this
> card and tap the chosen minions" takes effect, since all of it's "targets"
> (if they are indeed targets for that part of the effect) are not around?

No, since it is not optional.

Blessing of the Name doesn't say "you may burn this card and tap the chosen
minions".

On May 6, 3:47 pm, Blooded Sand <sandm...@gmail.com> wrote:

My point was that the Norman's deck was too low on permanent votes to
act like a voting deck. Some of its votes are usually hard to push
(especially Dogs of War), and the used transient votes package (4
Bewitchings + 6 Iron Glare) isn't going to help much, especially
without Bronwen.
I'm NOT trying to say that these cards are weak. I just think that
they are "cards to make the rich one even more rich": they help to
push your votes if you already have a decent number of permanent
votes. They also aid Voter Captivations. But if you don't have perma-
votes, you should replace these cards with Awe. Furthermore, I'd
suggest dropping Auto-da-fe and reducing number of Voter Captivations.

IG would be much more logical here ("make the rich one more rich"). I
will think about it.
Considering the allies possibility: it depends on the action, right?
If you're trying to push Dogs of War that allows ALL your vampires to
rush ANY other and diablerize freely, you aren't likely to make other
players support you, unless you split the table. But Trumpet-Up
Charges isn't that global: you just want to kill one vampire. Your
grandpredator should be happy if you select a vampire of his prey. A
rush player may be happy to have a permanent possibility of cycling
combat cards. And so on.
